question.text: A Category III AIF discharges tax on its income at the fund level through the trustee or fund acting as representative assessee. What is the consequence for ON-DISTRIBUTION cashflows to a resident individual investor?

answer.text: 10% TDS under Section 194LBB on all distributions
No further tax on the distribution because the fund/trustee has already discharged fund-level tax as representative assessee

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that, because Category III AIFs do not have pass-through status, the fund or trustee discharges tax on income at the fund level as representative assessee. Once that tax has been paid, there is no further investor-level tax on distribution or redemption proceeds attributable to that already-taxed income. The Trap: Option A applies the Section 194LBB withholding that the workbook prescribes for Investment Funds (Category I and II). Option B (Section 115A) is a non-resident provision. Option C (Section 194J) covers professional fees and is unrelated to fund distributions. Note: Because the fund has discharged tax upfront, investor statements should disclose the fund-level tax paid so that investors understand why no additional withholding appears at the distribution stage.
